robot-reinforcement-learning.title: Reinforcement Learning in Robotics: A Survey

language-generation.title: Survey of the State of the Art in Natural Language Generation: Core tasks, applications and evaluation

fairness-ml.title: Fairness and Machine Learning: Limitations and Opportunities — Introduction

relations.scope: Autoregressive language-model pretraining can learn by predicting tokens from surrounding text. This concerns a training stage, not every adaptation stage or every language-model design.
relations.rationale: Connect a model-family concept to the learning paradigm used in this pretraining example; do not classify all language-model training as self-supervised.

evidence.support: The paper describes autoregressive pretraining and explicitly discusses self-supervised prediction and its limits. The model release is evidence for a scoped method-use relation, not a new taxonomy node.

relations.scope: Neural generative implementations, including the multilayer-perceptron GAN example, use deep-learning methods. This is not a universal dependency, a synonym, or a claim that all generative methods are neural.
relations.rationale: Provide a useful cross-branch route from generation to one implementation family while retaining Generative AI as its existing Level 1 area.

evidence.support: The paper describes a generative model and discriminator implemented with multilayer perceptrons and trained by backpropagation. This supports the stated implementation example, not a universal hierarchy.

relations.scope: Robot-learning setups that improve behavior through reward feedback can use reinforcement learning. Robot learning also includes approaches that do not use reward-driven learning.
relations.rationale: Connect the robotics branch to a relevant learning paradigm without making the two concepts equivalent or changing either primary parent.

evidence.locator: Abstract and survey discussion of behavior generation
evidence.support: The authors survey reinforcement learning for robot behavior, including policy search and value-based methods, along with practical limits and prior knowledge.

relations.scope: The concepts intersect when a system produces natural-language text. This is not an equivalence: NLG also concerns input grounding, content planning, and organization, and may produce speech.
relations.rationale: Retain two independently placed canonical concepts while explaining their scoped intersection. No current, more precise non-hierarchical relation type expresses this intersection without overstating it.

evidence.locator: Abstract and overview of core NLG tasks
evidence.support: The survey describes generation of text or speech from non-linguistic input and the tasks and architectures involved. Mapping this intersection to the two AI Atlas concepts is a proposed editorial interpretation.

relations.scope: Bias and fairness analysis applies to machine-learning data, predictions, and deployment decisions in a social context. No single metric or successful check establishes fairness in every setting.
relations.rationale: Show a cross-cutting assessment concern without implying that fairness is a subclass of machine learning or that only machine-learning systems raise fairness concerns.

evidence.locator: Chapter 1: Introduction, especially the machine-learning loop and limitations
evidence.support: The authors examine disparities across the machine-learning decision process and explain the limits of technical fairness interventions in their surrounding social context.
